text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.6% today to $127.30, continuing a week-long slide that has erased 7.3% since mid-September. The timing and magnitude of the decline track closely with shifting geopolitical risk around Iran: last week's U.N. talks between Tehran and Washington sparked an 8% weekly drop in U.S. crude oil (now trading at $96.41 per barrel), and today's move follows Trump's reported rejection of Iran's conditional ceasefire proposal. When oil prices fall sharply, large integrated oil producers like ConocoPhillips see their earnings prospects dim, even if crude remains well above $90.

The backdrop here is messy geopolitical noise rather than a clean fundamental break. Saudi crude exports are hitting record highs despite infrastructure attacks, and the spread between U.S. and world oil prices remains wide (world crude at $114.89), which normally supports producer valuations—yet the market is clearly nervous about whether U.S.-Iran tensions will ease or escalate, making traders hesitant to hold the stock into that uncertainty.
